🇲🇽✊ <u>Mexico City's Unemployment Insurance Turns 20 With 550,000 Beneficiaries</u>

Twenty years ago Mexico City became the first entity in the country to pay people who lose their jobs. The Seguro de Desempleo started in 2007 under then-mayor Marcelo Ebrard, and it has since reached more than 550,000 beneficiaries, La Jornada reports. It averages 27,959 people a year. Over time it grew beyond laid-off workers: it has covered repatriated migrants, street vendors, market stallholders hit by fires or repairs, and victims of the 2017 earthquake.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex: No Mass Layoffs, No Wage Cuts</u>

Pemex called the reports of mass layoffs and lower salary scales false. The real 2026 headcount adjustment is 0.21% of the workforce, from eliminating duplicate posts and unnecessary hierarchy levels, with full severance and benefits paid under labor law, El Financiero reports. Salary scales stay as they are.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Morena to FGR: The CIA Probe Can't Stop at Jáuregui</u>

Morena leader Ariadna Montiel asked the FGR to widen the treason investigation over foreign agents in Chihuahua beyond ex-prosecutor César Jáuregui, to Governor Maru Campos herself, who signed a security agreement with the governor of Texas back in 2022. Campos had accused Montiel of narco ties in a private meeting with Sheinbaum, with no evidence. Montiel's answer: "If you have proof, present it."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>INE Contracts: No Shadow of Corruption, Says Sheinbaum</u>

With the 2027 electoral process already underway, Sheinbaum said there can be no shadow of corruption over the INE after videos showed its president, Guadalupe Taddei, alongside one of the institute's main contractors. "We all must take care of the institutions." Whether Taddei steps aside is her own call, she said, and this is not the old "don't touch the INE" crowd, who were protecting their own interests. Hours later the ASF opened an investigation, citing signs of irregularities in contracts and conflicts of interest.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Modalidad 40 Pension Fraud: Law Firms Under Federal Review</u>

Hacienda, the Anticorruption and Good Government ministry and the Presidency's Legal Counsel are now examining the law firms and institutions that helped people game IMSS's Modalidad 40 into pensions they had no right to, Sheinbaum said. Some of those pensions reach 80,000 to 90,000 pesos a month, paid with public money. The scheme was not cancelled; the IMSS Technical Council only shut the loopholes. A report with the number of improper beneficiaries and the damage to the treasury is coming.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>Rita Cetina Scholarship: Sign-Up Opens Oct 26</u>

SEP is notifying families: from October 26 to November 6, parents of kids in public primary and secondary schools can register for the Rita Cetina scholarship online at becaritacetina.gob.mx with their Llave MX. Secondary students get 1,900 pesos every two months, plus 700 for each additional sibling; primary students get a one-time 2,500 pesos. No middlemen, just a CURP and the school code.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>PAN Senator Hosts Israel's Ambassador to Talk Gaza "Disinformation"</u>

PAN senator Enrique Vargas del Villar met Israeli ambassador Yoed Magen at his liaison office in Huixquilucan last Thursday and posted the photo himself. On the agenda: "brotherhood with the Jewish people" and "disinformation" about Gaza. Days earlier, PRI and PAN figures crowned Israel's embassy "friendly diplomatic mission of the year" inside the Chamber of Deputies. Mexico, meanwhile, formally joined the genocide case against Israel at the ICJ.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>T-MEC Labor Case Closed: Nogales Plant Rehires Fired Union Workers</u>

Mexico's Economy Ministry and the US Trade Representative closed the T-MEC Rapid Response Labor Mechanism case at Amphenol Optimize México in Nogales, Sonora, which makes connectors and cables for the auto and aerospace industries. The company rehired nine workers it had fired without cause and paid all their back wages and benefits. It also issued a union-neutrality statement and set up a complaints channel. The union had reported coercion in a union vote in April 2025. Mexican authorities ran the review, trained workers in person, and opened anonymous reporting lines. Now that the case is closed, the plant's export shipments can be cleared normally again. (El Economista)

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum Shoots Down Loret's AMLO "Book Tour" Story</u>

Columnist Carlos Loret de Mola claimed former president López Obrador will tour Mexico from February to April 2027, at the peak of the election campaign, supposedly to promote his new book and boost Morena's candidates. President Sheinbaum called it false. She said AMLO is not going on tour and Morena is not paying for any book events. Then she added: "If he wanted to do a tour, what would be wrong with that?"

🇲🇽🏠 <u>Mexico City: 15,488 Housing Loans So Far This Year</u>

Clara Brugada handed out 3,317 housing benefits (home-improvement loans, loans for building new homes in stages, and property deeds) that reach more than 11,000 people. The home-improvement loans alone came to 2,381, worth 346 million pesos. The loans are interest-free and aimed at people shut out of bank credit. Housing Secretary Inti Muñoz said 15,488 loans have been approved this year, worth over 2.5 billion pesos, with a goal of 20,000 by December. Brugada said half the city has problems with its property titles, and set a target of 10,000 deeds for next year: "the right to decent housing and a legal patrimony for life."
